label: Agent Handoffs
summary: Cross-session handoff notes showing how conceptual Claude Code work became Codex implementation work.
description: Simulated notes kept by the developer after switching between coding agents, projects, and sessions.

items.label: Handoff: Brain evolution spec to implementation

data.summary: Claude Code defined the conceptual model for Brain evolution and Codex implemented it mostly as specified.
what_transferred_well: The list of allowed actions was concrete.
The event-driven surface gave Codex a clear integration point.
The rationale requirement made tests easier to design.
what_changed_during_execution: Codex discovered config updates needed merge semantics to avoid losing thresholds.
Split behavior needed a more constrained prompt than the initial spec provided.
data.developer_note: Best handoffs happen when Claude Code leaves both a concept and a small implementation contract.

data.summary: Claude Code scoped the product slice clearly, but Codex had to resolve browser-extension mechanics during implementation.
what_transferred_well: The capture payload fields were clear.
The decision to avoid collections and sharing kept the implementation small.
what_changed_during_execution: Selected text required content-script messaging and cached state.
The mocked persistence layer needed typed boundaries earlier than expected.
data.developer_note: For browser work, conceptual specs should mention extension lifecycle constraints because execution depends on them.

data.summary: Claude Code's product definition translated directly into Codex tests and implementation.
what_transferred_well: The 30 minute inactivity rule was precise.
The excluded event types were named before implementation.
The edge cases became a ready-made test list.
what_changed_during_execution: Codex discovered sessions must be grouped by account or visitor before timestamp sorting.
data.developer_note: When Claude Code defines acceptance cases, Codex can move quickly and catch hidden data-shape issues.

data.summary: Claude Code clarified the narrative purpose of the demo and Codex found the smallest data-driven implementation path.
what_transferred_well: The scenario requirements were concrete: agents, repos, sessions, handoffs.
The instruction to keep the first screen as the working demo matched the existing UI.
what_changed_during_execution: Codex avoided runtime changes because the existing data loader already supported the use case.
data.developer_note: For website demos, Claude Code is useful for story and information shape; Codex is better at fitting that story into the existing code path.

items.label: Handoff: agent memory taxonomy to importer

data.summary: Claude Code produced a useful taxonomy, but Codex had to make the schema stricter during importer implementation.
what_transferred_well: Agent identity, repo context, occasion, outcome, and handoff fields were already separated.
The taxonomy made it obvious that handoffs should be queryable.
what_changed_during_execution: Codex normalized agent names to prevent Claude, Claude Code, and claude-code from becoming separate concepts.
Handoff notes became structured metadata rather than only prose.
data.developer_note: Taxonomy sessions need a follow-up execution pass because schemas reveal ambiguities that conceptual work can hide.
